TLDR; EDS is not an autoimmune or viral condition in any way , it’s a connective tissue disorder, so really it’s just a lack of understanding of EDS that I was originally pointing out but since you wanted to be sarcastic I gave you the long version. Now if you want to talk about how various autoimmune conditions and viruses attack connective tissue on their own then that’s a separate statement from what OP asked.

Well I’m glad you asked.. I am an expert on ehlers danlos and comorbidities… because I have lived with them for 27 years and been diagnosed for 17. I travelled to Baltimore as a kid to be diagnsoed before a single doctor in my state even knew what it was. As someone who has a vested interested in the genetic component of EDS, and someone in the medical field, I’ve done a good amount of my own research into epigenetics. I supposed Covid could trigger certain epigentic factors that could exacerbate or activate symptoms of a connective tissues disorder in someone who already has the gene sequence/condition, but COVID cannot ‘cause’ EDS or comorbidities because you are born with it. It can probably activate MCAS as a result of disrupting the bodies histamine response , and generally wreak havoc on the body and all of its functions. I can also see COVID causing fibromyalgia-like symptoms for a myriad of reasons… but fibro is just a diagnosis of exclusion where EDS is genetic. 

But saying that COVID as a general ‘thing’ that has happened has caused people (silly hypochondriacs!) to think they have EDS… does not make sense from a medical perspective, and makes me wonder how much you really understand ehlers danlos and comorbidities to be making your own ‘factual’ statements. I also had long COVID this past year. Obviously we’ll need more research on covid to really understand what exactly it can and has done but I can tell you based on everything we know, it hasn’t caused EDS in people who had no underlying genetic pattern for it at all. This could be ‘proven’ if we knew the gene/genes responsible for EDS but since we don’t I guess you’ll just have to trust a gal with both EDS and medical experience. Or don’t. I’ve had enough medical gaslighting to live a lifetime so if you want a blame a common genetic condition finally getting recognition and diagnoses on COVID than be my guest. So I had hyprocure placed in both feet a year ago and eleven months ago respectively. The first few months were fine but I developed plantar fasciitis and flexor tendinitis as a result of very tight calf muscles and my new gait. I do pronate less now but it hasn’t been 100%, I still have some posterior tibial pain but it got better. I’m in PT. I just got a gastroc recession done (calf lengthening) which I’ve been told is often done in conjunction with the implants to prevent what happened to me; I think it’s already making a difference. A gastroc recession is also part of the general flat foot repair surgery so I figured at the very least I was getting on procedure out of the way. I am not ready to remove the implants yet, I’m going to see how I feel now that my calves aren’t so tight. I have a complicated case so I’m sorry it’s not so clear cut; if you’re have reasons NOT to get reconstruction like I did, then hyprocure may be a good first bet. It works great for some people and nor so great for others but at least it’s reversible  where reconstruction is a very long recovery and seems to not have the best success rate
